Non-Linear Optimization by a Trust-Region Method

Source: R/trust.R
trust.Rd

trust minimizes (or maximizes) a smooth objective function for which value, gradient and Hessian are available. It solves a Moré-Sorensen trust-region subproblem exactly, via the full eigendecomposition of the Hessian.

Usage

trust(
  objfun,
  parinit,
  rinit = 0.1,
  rmax = 10,
  iterlim = 1000L,
  hessianMethod = c("gn", "bfgs", "sr1", "exact"),
  phases = NULL,
  switches = NULL,
  parupper = NULL,
  parlower = NULL,
  boundary = c("reflective", "clip"),
  tolControl = NULL,
  qnControl = NULL,
  stepControl = NULL,
  minimize = TRUE,
  blather = FALSE,
  printIter = FALSE,
  traceFile = NULL,
  sparse = "auto",
  ...
)

trustL1(
  objfun,
  parinit,
  mu = 0 * parinit,
  one.sided = FALSE,
  lambda = 1,
  rinit = 0.1,
  rmax = 10,
  iterlim = 1000L,
  parupper = NULL,
  parlower = NULL,
  boundary = c("reflective", "clip"),
  tolControl = NULL,
  stepControl = NULL,
  minimize = TRUE,
  blather = FALSE,
  printIter = FALSE,
  traceFile = NULL,
  gate = NULL,
  fuse = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

objfun

Function whose first argument is a numeric vector of parameters, returning a list with components value, gradient and hessian. It is called with the logical arguments deriv and hessian, and with deriv2 = TRUE when an exact Hessian is requested, so it must accept them or ....

parinit

Named numeric starting vector. Must be finite. Values outside [parlower, parupper] are clipped with a warning; with boundary = "reflective" they are moved just inside the box.

rinit

Initial trust-region radius. Default 0.1.

rmax

Maximum trust-region radius. Default 10.

iterlim

Maximum number of trust-region iterations over all phases. Default 1000.

hessianMethod

Source of the model Hessian of a run without phases: "gn" (default) the Gauss-Newton Hessian of the objective, "bfgs" or "sr1" a quasi-Newton update seeded as qnControl$hessianInit says, "exact" the true Hessian at every iterate, which needs an objective that takes deriv2. Quasi-Newton methods require boundary = "reflective". Also selects the control defaults below. With phases, each phase names a method, and this argument is an error.

phases

List of phases, each a list of settings, run one after the other and from the first again after the last. The run hands over to the next phase at a value, model, step or stagnation stop and when a phase uses up the iterlim of that phase. A handover restarts the trust region at rinit and discards the quasi-Newton pairs. Default NULL: one phase from hessianMethod and qnControl, evaluated with the sweep in .... Names of the list label the phases in the result, the Hessian source does otherwise. Not available with multiple shooting and boundary = "clip".

hessianMethod

Hessian source of the phase, as hessianMethod. Required.

iterlim

Maximum number of iterations of one run of the phase. Default NULL: only the total iterlim.

sweep

"forward" or "reverse", the sweep the objective is evaluated with in the phase; a sweep in ... is an error with phases. Default NULL: for "bfgs" and "sr1" reverse if the objective can be evaluated backwards at parinit, as with derivMode = c("forward", "reverse") throughout the chain, forward otherwise. A Gauss-Newton Hessian is always computed forward. A handover between phases of different sweep evaluates the current iterate once more. The result reports the sweeps as phaseSweep.

qnControl

Quasi-Newton settings of the phase, merged over qnControl; see there. hessianInit defaults to "gn" in every phase but the first: a quasi-Newton phase starts from the Gauss-Newton Hessian at the iterate of the handover.

switches

Number of handovers allowed. Default NULL: one fewer than there are phases, so each runs once. A higher value cycles through the phases again, 0 runs the first phase only. The result reports the count as nSwitch.

parupper, parlower

Upper and lower bounds. Unnamed: the first element applies to all parameters. Named: entries are matched by name, missing parameters are unbounded. Default NULL, unbounded.

boundary

Box-bound handling, "reflective" (default) or "clip". See section Box bounds.

tolControl

List of convergence thresholds, merged into the defaults.

ftol

Change in objective value. Default 1e-6.

mtol

Predicted model decrease. Default 1e-6.

gtol

First-order optimality measure. Default 1e-6.

xtol

Step norm. Default 0, disabled.

rmin

Lower limit on the trust radius; falling below it stops the run with converged = FALSE. Default 0, disabled.

ctol

Multiple shooting only: scaled gap size below which the trajectory counts as continuous; no other test stops the run before. Default 1e-6.

trustL1 reads ftol, mtol, gtol, xtol and rmin.

qnControl

List of quasi-Newton settings, merged into the defaults and read only in a "bfgs" or "sr1" phase.

hessianInit

Seed of the approximation: "gn" (default) the Gauss-Newton Hessian at parinit; "identity" the identity matrix, after which no Hessian is requested from the objective; "exact" the true Hessian at parinit, then gradients only. "exact" needs deriv2, see derivMode in odemodel(). Used only when hessianMethod is "bfgs" or "sr1".

hessianReseed

"never" (default): a stalled quasi-Newton phase, or one whose trust radius collapses, stops. "stall": it continues from a fresh Hessian of the same source at the current iterate, provided the iterate moved since the last reseed. The result reports the count as nReseed.

qnMemory

Number of (s, y) pairs kept. Default 0: every update accumulates onto the seed. A positive value rebuilds the approximation in each iteration from the last qnMemory pairs, without the seed.

qnCautious

A BFGS pair is used only when \(s^\top y > c\,|s|\,|y|\) with \(c\) = qnCautious. Default 1e-8, 0 disables the test; "sr1" is exempt. The result reports the rejected pairs as qnSkipped.

qnRejected

Whether "sr1" also updates from a rejected trial point. Default TRUE for a phase whose source is "sr1", FALSE otherwise.

stepControl

List of step and acceptance settings, merged into the defaults.

thetaMax

Largest fraction of the distance to a bound a step may use. Default 0.99995. boundary = "reflective" only.

nonmonotone

Zhang-Hager relaxation in [0, 1): a step is rated against a weighted average of past objective values and may increase the objective. Default 0, monotone.

acceptance

Multiple shooting only: "filter" (default), the filter of Fletcher and Leyffer on objective and gap size; "merit", the l2 exact penalty; "natural", Bock's natural level function, which needs hessianMethod = "gn", a fixed sigma and no error model.

twoPhase

Multiple shooting only: if TRUE, the parameters are first fitted with the node values held fixed, then the nodes are laid out afresh and released. Default FALSE.

restore

Multiple shooting only: if TRUE, a run whose steps keep being rejected with open gaps enters a restoration phase, at most five times. Default FALSE.

regularize

Multiple shooting only: directions of the condensed problem with a singular value below regularize times the largest are held fixed in a step. Default 0, off. With acceptance = "natural" directions below 1e-7 are always held fixed.

soc

Multiple shooting only: if TRUE, a rejected step whose gaps did not close as predicted is retried once with a second-order correction. Default TRUE.

anneal

Multiple shooting only: if TRUE, the run first minimizes the objective plus a rising penalty on the gaps, then enforces continuity. Needs forward sensitivities and is skipped without them. Default TRUE.

minimize

If TRUE (default) minimize, if FALSE maximize.

blather

If TRUE, the result also contains the per-iteration trace listed under Value. Default FALSE.

printIter

If TRUE, print iteration count and objective value at each evaluation. Default FALSE.

traceFile

Path of a CSV file written with one row per evaluation: iteration, objective value and parameters. Default NULL, no file.

sparse

"auto" (default), TRUE or FALSE. With TRUE, objfun is called with hessian = "sparse" and the sparse Gauss-Newton Hessian it returns (a Matrix) is factorized by sparse Cholesky. Without phases and bounds; of the other settings only rinit, rmax, iterlim, tolControl$ftol, tolControl$mtol and printIter apply. "auto" takes this path for a Gauss-Newton minimization without phases, bounds, exact Hessian, trace or multiple shooting when parinit has at least parameters entries and the sparse Hessian at parinit fills at most fill of the matrix, both from getOption("dMod2.sparseAuto"), a list that defaults to parameters = 500 and fill = 0.05.

...

Further named arguments passed to objfun.

mu

Named numeric vector of reference values for the L1-penalized parameters. Names must be a subset of names(parinit); only the named parameters receive a penalty. Each must lie strictly inside [parlower, parupper]. Defaults to a zero vector covering all of parinit.

one.sided

Logical. If TRUE, the penalty is one-sided and acts as a lower wall at mu: lambda * max(0, mu - p). Otherwise it is the symmetric lambda * |p - mu|.

lambda

Strength of the L1 penalty. Either a scalar (broadcast to all entries of mu) or a named numeric aligned with mu.

gate

Character, names in mu whose penalty is the gate lambda * (p - mu) with p >= mu: the parameter can sit exactly on mu and leaves it only upward. Starts below mu are moved onto it.

fuse

List of fusion blocks. A block penalizes lambda * sum_{i<j} w_ij |p_i - p_j| over the parameters of the block, plus lambda * w_ia |p_i - a| toward an optional anchor a. Parameters with equal values move as one and split again when the data pull them apart. A block is a character vector of parameter names or a list with pars, and optionally lambda (default: the scalar lambda), anchor (default none) and weights, an (m+1) x (m+1) matrix whose last row and column refer to the anchor (default all 1). Fused parameters must not appear in mu; if fuse is given and mu is not, mu is empty.

Value

A list of class trustfit with components

argument

Named numeric, the best iterate.

value, gradient, hessian

Objective value, gradient and model Hessian at argument.

iterations

Number of iterations.

neval

Number of objective evaluations.

qnEval

Evaluations spent in a quasi-Newton phase.

qnSkipped

Pairs rejected by the cautious test.

nSwitch

Number of handovers between phases.

phaseIterations

Named integer, the iterations of each phase run, in run order and named after the phase; sums to iterations.

phaseSweep

Named character, the sweep of each element of phases, present when phases is set.

nReseed

Number of reseeds by qnControl$hessianReseed = "stall", which allows each run of a phase the same number.

evalBySource

Named integer, evaluations per Hessian source.

converged

Logical.

atBound

Named logical, the parameters held by a bound.

stopReason

The test that ended the run, see section Convergence.

With blather = TRUE the list also contains the matrices argpath (accepted iterates) and argtry (trial points), one row per iteration, and the per-iteration vectors steptype, stepback, accept, r (radius), rho (ratio of actual to predicted reduction), valpath, valtry, preddiff, stepnorm and, when a quasi-Newton source is involved, hessianSource.

boundary = "clip" returns only argument, value, gradient, hessian, iterations, converged, atBound and stopReason, plus the trace.

A multiple-shooting run returns argument, value, gradient, hessian, iterations, neval, qnSkipped, converged, stopReason, atBound and a list multipleShooting with the final nodes, the gaps per condition, their scaled size violation, the counts nRelaxed (iterations with a node step below the full one), nSOC (accepted second-order corrections), nSplit (segments cut), nRestore (restoration phases) and nStages (annealing stages), the cuts, the acceptance and sweep used, mu (merit) or filterSize (filter), and trace when blather = TRUE.

Box bounds

boundary = "reflective" (default) uses the interior trust-region-reflective scheme of Coleman and Li. Iterates stay strictly inside the box and never land exactly on a bound; atBound in the result reports which parameters a bound holds.

boundary = "clip": active-set reduction with componentwise clipping.

Convergence

The run stops as soon as one of the following holds. The gradient test is evaluated at the current iterate; the value and step tests count only on an accepted step, the model test also on a rejected Newton step from inside the trust region.

  • gtol: the first-order optimality measure \(\max_i |v_i g_i|\) is at most gtol, with \(v_i\) the distance to the bound the gradient points to, 1 if that bound is infinite. Without bounds it is \(\max_i |g_i|\).

  • ftol: \(|f - f_{\mathrm{try}}| <\) ftol.

  • mtol: the predicted reduction \(|g^\top p + \frac{1}{2} p^\top H p| <\) mtol.

  • xtol: the step norm is below xtol.

  • stagnation: five consecutive rejected steps left the objective flat within ftol.

  • rmin: the trust radius is below rmin, or a step no longer changes the parameters in floating point. Reports converged = FALSE.

stopReason in the result names the test that fired: "gradient", "fvalue", "preddiff", "step", "stagnation", "radius", "objfun" (three failed evaluations in a row) or "iterlim". Stagnation reports converged = TRUE.

Only gtol tests first-order optimality. While switches remain, see phases, an "fvalue", "preddiff", "step" or "stagnation" stop hands over to the next phase instead of ending the run. In a quasi-Newton phase "fvalue", "preddiff" and "step" do not end the run. A phase that reaches the iterlim of that phase ends like a soft stop, with stopReason = "iterlim" and converged = FALSE when no handover is left. The total iterlim ends the run in any phase, with stopReason = "iterlim" and converged = FALSE.

argument, value, gradient, hessian and atBound in the result belong to the best iterate visited, which is the last accepted one when stepControl$nonmonotone = 0.

Multiple shooting

An objective built by normL2(..., multipleShootingControl = ), alone or in a sum, is optimized by multiple shooting with the same controls. Not available then: hessianMethod = "exact", more than one phase, switches, qnControl$hessianReseed, qnControl$qnMemory, stepControl$nonmonotone, boundary = "clip", minimize = FALSE and traceFile. The run reports converged = TRUE only when the scaled gaps between the segments are below tolControl$ctol. The method is described in the methods article Multiple shooting.

References

Coleman, T. F. and Li, Y. (1996). An interior trust region approach for nonlinear minimization subject to bounds. SIAM Journal on Optimization 6(2), 418-445.

Fröhlich, F. and Sorger, P. K. (2022). Fides: Reliable trust-region optimization for parameter estimation of ODE models. PLoS Computational Biology 18(7), e1010322.

Bock, H. G. (1983). Recent advances in parameter identification techniques for ODE. In Numerical Treatment of Inverse Problems in Differential and Integral Equations, 95-121. Birkhäuser.

Fletcher, R. and Leyffer, S. (2002). Nonlinear programming without a penalty function. Mathematical Programming 91, 239-269.

Horbelt, W., Timmer, J. and Voss, H. U. (2002). Parameter estimation in nonlinear delayed feedback systems from noisy data. Physics Letters A 299, 513-521.

Voss, H. U., Timmer, J. and Kurths, J. (2004). Nonlinear dynamical system identification from uncertain and indirect measurements. International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos 14(6), 1905-1933.

Peifer, M. and Timmer, J. (2007). Parameter estimation in ordinary differential equations for biochemical processes using the method of multiple shooting. IET Systems Biology 1(2), 78-88.

See also

mstrust() for multi-start fits, profile() for profile likelihoods, normL2() for the objective, the guide chapter Optimization, the methods article Trust-region optimization.

Examples

rosenbrock <- function(x, ...) {
  a <- x[["a"]]
  b <- x[["b"]]
  list(value = 100 * (b - a^2)^2 + (1 - a)^2,
       gradient = c(a = -400 * a * (b - a^2) - 2 * (1 - a),
                    b = 200 * (b - a^2)),
       hessian = matrix(c(1200 * a^2 - 400 * b + 2, -400 * a, -400 * a, 200),
                        2, 2, dimnames = list(c("a", "b"), c("a", "b"))))
}

fit <- trust(rosenbrock, c(a = -1.2, b = 1), iterlim = 200)
fit$argument
#> a b 
#> 1 1 
fit$stopReason
#> [1] "fvalue"

# With an upper bound on a
fit <- trust(rosenbrock, c(a = -1.2, b = 1), parupper = c(a = 0.5),
             iterlim = 200)
fit$atBound
#>     a     b 
#>  TRUE FALSE 

# Gauss-Newton, then BFGS with a separate budget, then Gauss-Newton again
fit <- trust(rosenbrock, c(a = -1.2, b = 1), iterlim = 200,
             phases = list(list(hessianMethod = "gn"),
                           list(hessianMethod = "bfgs", iterlim = 50)),
             switches = 2)
fit$phaseIterations
#>   gn bfgs 
#>   26    0 
fit$evalBySource
#>    gn  bfgs   sr1 exact 
#>    27     0     0     0
